workload.source: read-only SWE-rebench offline training seed clause-lattice-time-kb.json
workload.sequence: Begin four overlapping Edge calls, complete in reverse order, enqueue their Lattice batch, wait for worker completion, query Lattice; repeat eight times, then explicitly save.
workload.labels_and_features: Original recorded values; incoming timestamps rebased to be causal after training.
workload.timed_region: Online learning and queries plus one final durable save; excludes corpus load, fitting, seed creation and restore setup.

method.processes: Separate fresh processes, sequential; no validation or heavy diagnostics ran concurrently.
method.baseline_setup: git archive 511de1d3db86a868328ff1cce7df2b26fec294ef services/sidecar/src contracts, extracted to a separate directory

equivalence.fingerprint_scope: Every recorded Lattice/Edge prediction plus final Lattice, Edge (including runtime tokens/feedback/weights), Trie and Runtime snapshots. Trie/Runtime are static in this writer workload.
equivalence.reload_checks: Saved Edge payload equals live state; restored Edge model equals live nodes/edges; restored Lattice future prediction equals live prediction. Overlapping feedback after restart is also checked in test_kb_checkpoint_policy.py.

validation_notes: Full suite: all tests except one PATH-dependent subprocess test passed; two opt-in Docker/cgroup checks skipped.
Follow-up includes that subprocess test with the venv on PATH, the new normal-close test, predictor, writer, Edge runtime, lifecycle and HTTP API suites after the final close change.
New test/probe Ruff checks pass; changed production modules have 50 pre-existing findings and no added findings relative to baseline.
Unrun live checks and commands are recorded in docs/CURRENT_PLAN.md.
limits: This is a model/writer component replay, not a full HTTP concurrency or long-duration acceptance test.
The final checkpoint is still a full snapshot and generation copy; its cost remains proportional to model size.
This 2048-row history produces a roughly 48 MB changed snapshot payload; do not extrapolate its timings to the earlier 2.08 GB full corpus.
Peak RSS includes setup, snapshot verification, and both live/restored models; it is not steady-state service memory.

Retention, Lattice reindexing, query locks, and memory growth are unchanged. Earlier update visibility can change wall-clock query results while preserving the algorithm for identical visible history.
Forced termination loses learning since the last completed explicit save, as authorized.
